## The carry of energy and momentum with withheld mass {#sec-ch08-carry}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
- Mass the limiter withholds must not leave its energy and momentum behind.
- Switch: the same as the limiter, and only where the equation of state defines a species enthalpy.
- The withheld mass of a face takes the enthalpy and velocity of that face's donor.
- The $x_1$ flux is split into an advected and a settling part, each with its own donor.
:::

The limiter of @sec-ch08-theta scales a species mass flux down. That mass does not vanish: it stays in
the donor cell. If the energy and momentum fluxes are left unscaled, the mass stays behind but its
enthalpy and momentum leave, and the cell loses energy it still holds. This section is the correction
that keeps the books straight.

The outline carries this scheme twice, as 8.2 and 8.3, from two inventories. They describe the same
mechanism and are merged here into one section.

### Derivation

Write the unscaled face flux of species $n$ as $F$, and let $\theta_d$ be the factor of that face's
donor. The limiter replaces $F$ by $\theta_d F$, so the mass withheld at that face is

$$
\mathrm{d}m = (1 - \theta_d)\,F .
$$ {#eq-ch08-carry-dm}

The energy flux of the face must lose $\mathrm{d}m\,h_{\mathrm{spec}}$ and the momentum flux
$\mathrm{d}m\,v$, both evaluated **at the donor**, because that is the cell the mass did not leave.

`[C6]` checks precisely that correspondence rather than restating @eq-ch08-carry-dm: it computes the
energy the withheld mass would have carried as the difference between the unscaled and scaled mass
flux times the donor's enthalpy, independently of the expression the code uses, and compares. The two
agree to $1.8\times10^{-15}$ in energy and $8.9\times10^{-16}$ in momentum over two thousand face sets.

The donor is chosen per face and per part of the flux, not per cell. In $x_1$ the flux carries two
physically distinct pieces, an advected part and a settling part from sedimentation, and they need not
move in the same direction: a species may be advected upward while settling downward through the same
face. Each part therefore takes its own donor, which is why the code applies the withholding twice in
$x_1$ and once elsewhere.

### Numerical method

The carry is `flux_positivity_carry_` at [`flux_positivity.cpp:106-149`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp#L106-L149). The withheld share
is taken from the *net* flux's donor at `theta` ([`flux_positivity.cpp:124-125`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp#L124-L125)), matching the choice
`flux_positivity_scale_` made, so the mass that was actually withheld is the mass that is accounted
for. The energy and momentum subtraction is `part` ([`flux_positivity.cpp:127-135`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp#L127-L135)), with the
enthalpy and velocity taken from the lower or upper cell according to the sign of the part being
withheld.

The $x_1$ split is `sed` ([`flux_positivity.cpp:136-143`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp#L136-L143)): when a sedimentation flux is given, the
advected part is the net flux minus it, and `withhold` is called once on each. The other two
directions have no settling flux and take the single branch.

The species enthalpy comes from the equation of state at `species_enthalpy` ([`hydro_forward.cpp:675-677`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L675-L677)),
computed on the primitive state with ghosts included. The code comment there records that exchanging
it alongside the factors changed no bit, so it is not exchanged; that is a measurement someone made,
not a derivation, and it is recorded as such.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- The carry runs only where the equation of state defines a species enthalpy. With an equation of
  state that does not, the limiter still withholds mass and the energy is not corrected, so the two
  mechanisms are not switched together.
:::

1. **Kinetic energy.** The withheld energy is the species enthalpy times the mass. Whether the kinetic
   energy of the withheld mass is accounted for consistently with the momentum correction is not
   something this chapter measures, and no test in the repository isolates it.
2. **Hypothesis.** That the settling and advected parts need separate donors because they can move in
   opposite directions is an argument from the physics of sedimentation and from the shape of the code.
   No test in the repository constructs a face where the two parts disagree in sign.
